title: Launch Brief (Slides) — Optimize: Quantization Profile Library (Opt-in, Route-Scoped) — Beta
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Quantization Profile Library (Beta)
Opt-in, route-scoped quantization profiles for lower unit cost with safety rails

Speaker notes:
- This is the beta launch brief for the Quantization Profile Library.
- Core theme: cost reduction without “surprise regressions,” by making adoption controlled and observable.


Slide 2 — What we’re shipping (one sentence)
We will publish Redwood-verified quantization profiles per model (e.g., fp16/bf16/int8/int4 variants) and let customers enable them per API route with canaries + fast rollback.

Speaker notes:
- Library is Redwood-published only in v1 (no user-supplied profiles).
- Route-scoped toggles are the primary adoption mechanism.


Slide 3 — Why now (customer + platform drivers)
Customer drivers
- Unit cost pressure is rising as LLM features expand (summarization, agents, batch pipelines)
- Teams want predictable performance gains + safety controls (esp. enterprise)
- Strong preference for “enable on background routes first” pattern

Platform drivers
- Runtime + registry investments make it feasible to standardize profiles + validation
- We have enough telemetry and routing primitives to safely gate via policy + canary

Speaker notes:
- We are not trying to win “most knobs”; we are trying to remove fear of adoption.


Slide 4 — Positioning (external / internal)
External positioning (customer-facing)
- “Safer cost optimization”: opt-in, route-level control, with Redwood-verified profiles
- “Production-ready quantization”: profiles scoped to hardware/kernels + validated evals

Internal positioning (what this enables)
- A standardized artifact lifecycle for quantized variants across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
- A foundation for future automation (more models, broader hardware, smarter recommendations)

Speaker notes:
- Avoid framing as a generic quantization feature; this is an operational product surface.


Slide 5 — Target beta audience (who should get access)
Ideal beta candidates
- High token-volume workloads with clear segmentation between interactive vs batch routes
- Existing Redwood Optimize users (or customers actively engaged on cost reduction)
- Teams with stable prompt sets / known eval expectations (can produce success signal)

Non-ideal for beta
- Teams requiring strict output format guarantees on every request without tolerance bands
- Workloads with frequent prompt changes and no regression monitoring

Speaker notes:
- We can still support some JSON-mode routes, but we should be conservative in onboarding.


Slide 6 — Primary beta use cases
Recommended first routes (low-risk)
- Background summarization / report generation
- Offline classification / enrichment (async)
- Embeddings + reranking workloads where supported

Later routes (higher scrutiny)
- Interactive chat (latency + quality sensitivity)
- Tool-calling / strict JSON output routes
- Long-context workloads (higher variance; perf regressions possible)


Slide 7 — What “Quantization Profile Library” means (customer mental model)
Concepts
- Profile: a versioned, signed, hardware-scoped “recipe” for running a model variant (e.g., int8)
- Route controls: choose whether that route can use quantized execution, and at what canary %
- Safe fallback: baseline kernels remain available; incompatibility or guardrails trigger baseline

Customer promise (beta)
- Quantization never becomes default-on without explicit enablement
- Clear visibility: route shows whether traffic is quantized vs baseline


Slide 8 — MVP scope (Beta)
Included
- Redwood-published profiles for an initial set of high-demand models (limited matrix)
- Route-level enable/disable + canary percentage
- Audit logs for config changes
- Metrics tagging: profile id/version + quantized/baseline execution mode
- Rollback runbook + auto-disable hooks (where signals exist)

Explicitly NOT in beta
- Customer-supplied profiles
- “Always-on” quantization for all customers
- Fully automated profile generation for every new model without review

Speaker notes:
- Keep beta narrow; the goal is safe adoption + operational maturity.


Slide 9 — Release strategy (opt-in and progressive exposure)
Access model
- Feature flag / allowlist for beta orgs
- Console + API surface (same underlying config)

Rollout model per customer
1) Enable on a single background route at 1–5% canary
2) Monitor quality + format adherence + latency
3) Ramp to 25% / 50% / 100% if stable
4) Expand to additional routes (do not “flip everything”)

Speaker notes:
- “Route segmentation” is the key adoption pattern we should coach.


Slide 10 — Success metrics (Beta) — what we’ll measure
North-star: meaningful unit cost reduction without unacceptable quality regressions

Product KPIs
- Cost improvement: median tokens/$ improvement on enabled routes (target: +20% or better on supported profiles)
- Adoption: % of beta orgs enabling quantization on >= 1 route (target: 30–40% within 30 days of beta access)
- Retention: % of enabled routes still enabled after 14 days (target: 80%+)

Quality / safety KPIs
- Regression rate: % of enabled routes requiring rollback due to quality/format issues (target: <10%)
- Incident rate: sev2+ incidents attributable to quantization profile issues (target: 0)
- Auto-disable accuracy: % of auto-disables that correspond to real customer-visible degradation (target: tracked; improve over time)

Performance KPIs
- p95 latency delta on enabled routes (target: non-regressive; accept small variance if cost wins are strong and customer agrees)
- 5xx increase attributable to quantized path (target: none; any increase is a rollback trigger)

Speaker notes:
- For beta, we can accept “mixed outcomes” as long as rollback is fast and safe.


Slide 11 — Beta entry criteria (go/no-go gates)
Engineering readiness
- Runtime profile resolution + compatibility checks are in place
- Baseline fallback path is proven (mismatch => baseline)
- Cache stampede protections verified in load test

Quality + validation readiness
- Initial profiles pass acceptance thresholds (eval + perf)
- Perf suite run across supported GPU SKUs for target sequence length bins

Operational readiness
- Dashboards exist and segment by route + profile + execution mode
- SRE runbook approved; oncall escalation path defined
- Audit logs validated; config changes are reversible

Documentation readiness
- Customer docs drafted: how to enable, how to canary, how to rollback
- Known limitations clearly stated


Slide 12 — Support readiness checklist (Customer Success + Support)
Before enabling for a customer
- Confirm supported deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and GPU availability
- Confirm route candidates (background vs interactive) and recommended canary plan
- Confirm customer understands “beta” constraints + rollback expectations

During beta
- Weekly check-in with beta orgs (10–15 min) on outcomes + issues
- Fast path for disabling per route/customer
- Capture: which prompts/routes are sensitive; feed into prompt-set expansion plan

Tooling needed
- One-click link from route settings to “quantization metrics” view
- A standard “triage checklist” for JSON-mode/tool-calling regressions

Speaker notes:
- We should reduce back-and-forth by giving Support a crisp triage decision tree.


Slide 13 — Messaging & doc plan (what we’ll say)
Terminology
- Prefer “quantization profile” over “preset/variant” (avoid confusion with model versions)

Customer-facing copy themes
- “Enable per route”
- “Canary before ramp”
- “Rollback in seconds”
- “Hardware-scoped, Redwood-verified profiles”

Docs artifacts
- Quickstart: enable quantization for a route + canary
- Monitoring guide: which dashboards matter
- Troubleshooting guide: format regressions, long-context perf, incompatibility fallback

Speaker notes:
- Consistency matters across Console, docs, and support responses.


Slide 14 — Risks & mitigations (beta-specific)
Risk: workload-specific quality regressions
- Mitigation: route-level canaries + conservative defaults + prompt-set coverage expansion

Risk: hardware/kernel compatibility surprises
- Mitigation: explicit hardware scoping, runtime compatibility checks, baseline fallback

Risk: operational complexity (config precedence, auditing)
- Mitigation: clear precedence rules, audit logs, reversible changes, documented runbook

Risk: telemetry/billing attribution errors
- Mitigation: quantized/baseline tagging + validation checks in pre-prod; alert if missing tags

Speaker notes:
- “Safe failure mode” must be baseline, not error.


Slide 15 — Rollout timeline (proposed 10–12 weeks)
Weeks 1–2
- PRD + design sign-off; schema decisions; pick initial model set + supported hardware

Weeks 3–6
- Registry artifacts + runtime resolution + route policy controls (behind flags)

Weeks 5–8
- Validation pipeline (eval + perf), telemetry tags, dashboards, rollback tooling

Weeks 9–10
- Dedicated/Private compatibility testing; docs + SDK guidance

Weeks 11–12
- Limited beta (opt-in) + expand supported models; GA decision using KPIs

Speaker notes:
- Some work streams overlap intentionally; perf + eval gating should be continuous.


Slide 16 — Beta operating cadence (how we run it)
Weekly
- Beta cohort status: enabled routes, cost wins, regressions, rollbacks
- Profile pipeline status: profiles in review, blocked items, next GPU targets

Bi-weekly
- Cross-functional review: Product + Applied ML + Runtime + SRE
- Decide: expand cohort vs stabilize

Exit criteria (toward GA)
- Stable rollback/disable experience across multiple orgs
- Repeatable profile publish workflow
- Measurable cost wins with regression rate within target bands


Slide 17 — Open questions (needs decisions)
- Initial model list: which 2–4 models provide fastest customer value with manageable risk?
- Which workloads are “approved for beta” vs “case-by-case” (JSON-mode, tool-calling)?
- Packaging: included in Optimize beta by request, or separate allowlist regardless of Optimize?
- Who owns beta onboarding: Solutions Eng vs CS vs Product?
- Default canary % recommendation (5%?) and ramp schedule guidance

Speaker notes:
- Align early; otherwise we’ll burn cycles on inconsistent onboarding.


Slide 18 — Asks / next steps
Product
- Confirm beta cohort selection criteria and packaging language
- Approve success metrics and beta exit criteria

Engineering (Runtime/Platform)
- Confirm feature-flag strategy and precedence rules are final
- Confirm telemetry tags required for dashboards + alerts

Applied ML / Evals
- Confirm acceptance thresholds for initial profiles
- Confirm prompt-set additions for quantization sensitivity

SRE/Support
- Approve rollback runbook + alert thresholds
- Identify oncall rotation + escalation path for beta

Owner: Aditya Rao | Program: Talia Benson
